correctness.rationale: A closed-neighborhood identifying code C is exactly a mask whose 14 bitwise neighborhood intersections are nonempty and pairwise different. Since there are 2^14=16384 masks, enumerating all 0<=|C|<=7 is complete: no masks size<=6 qualify, exactly 268 size-seven codes qualify. A legal slide between two codes changes exactly one chosen vertex to an adjacent nonchosen vertex, equivalent to two bits in the XOR and adjacency of the two changed vertices. Independent full-pair enumeration yields precisely 210 slide edges; connected components have sizes 4 (56) and 22 (2), with degree fingerprints (1,1,1,3) and (1 repeated 21,21), forcing the claimed star forest. This is a true finite exhaustive proof, with no extrapolation to other Heawood-like graphs.

value.rationale: Identifying codes are a standard natural code invariant on the canonical Fano incidence graph; token-slide connectivity encodes local reconfiguration feasibility. The complete star-forest fragmentation, despite an existing much more connected unrestricted token-jump graph, is a meaningful finite structural graph classification rather than just another code count.

final_claim: For the 14-vertex Fano incidence graph, the complete adjacency-restricted token-slide reconfiguration graph of its 268 minimum size-seven identifying codes is 56 K_(1,3) disjoint union 2 K_(1,21), totaling 210 edges and 58 components.
limitations: All-state finite classification is rigorous for one fixed 14-vertex graph, not a higher-order asymptotic claim.
